the mafic rocks in the central part Lhasa Terranes were generated from the Neo-Thetys slab breakoff, and the slab breakoff occurred at ca. 57 Ma in the central part Tibet.

The main takeaway from our work is that

subduction-related magmatic processes were sustained during the transition from Neo-Tethys subduction to continental India-Asia collision, and that the subduction zone remained active until ca. 50 Ma.

the Neo-Tethyian slab continued to influence the mantle wedge after the initial India-Asia continental collisions, which may have contributed to the generation of magmas that were subsequently emplaced in the Lhasa Terran.
the Neo-Tethan slab was a significant heat source during continental collision, even after the initiation of continental collision and prior to slab breakoff.
